steps_raw.instruction: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid V (ACSF.V)
Scope and Applicability: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid is used during surgical procedures to maintain tissue hydration and minimize tissue damage, adhesion formation and infection.
Sodium Chloride (NaCl; VWR JT4058 or equivalent)
Potassium Chloride (KCl; Sigma P9333 or equivalent)
Magnesium Chloride (MgCl2; VWR 80503-016 or equivalent)
Calcium Chloride dihydrate (CaCl2 • 2H2O; Sigma C3306 or equivalent)
HEPES (Sigma H3375 or equivalent)
Potassium Hydroxide (1N KOH in water; Acros Organics AC27840-0010 or equivalent)
MilliQ Water (RNase-free)
Labeled 1 Liter plastic bottle (or equivalent as directed by project lead's request)
1000 ml graduated cylinder
25 ml serological pipette
1 liter filter system, 0.22 µm (Corning 431206 purchased as VWR 28199-812 or equivalent)
Disposable plastic spatulas
Gast vacuum pump (Model # DOA-P104-AA or equivalent)
Magnetic stir bar remover
KOH can cause burns. Wear proper PPE including gloves and eye protection while handling this chemical. Use this chemical in a fume hood.
Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid (ACSF) containing:
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Obtain a sterile 1 liter plastic bottle. Label the container with the reagent name, date and your initials.
Obtain an RNase free stir bar and add to the container.
Ensure pH meter is calibrated.
Ensure balance is calibrated.
Methodology/Procedures (record all lot numbers and volumes used in the appropriate reagent prep notebook):
To make 1000 ml of Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid (ACSF):
Using a graduated cylinder, measure and add 900 ml of MilliQ water to an appropriately labeled RNase free container containing an RNase free stir bar.
Place container on stir plate and begin stirring at a high setting (7 or higher).
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 7.889 g of Sodium Chloride (NaCl). Slowly add weighed NaCl to the container while stirring.
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 403 mg of Potassium Chloride (KCl). Slowly add weighed KCl to the container while stirring.
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 203 mg of Magnesium Chloride (MgCl2). Slowly add weighed MgCl2 to the container while stirring.
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 265 mg of Calcium Chloride (CaCl2). Slowly add weighed CaCl2 to the container while stirring.
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 1.192 g of HEPES. Slowly add weighed HEPES to the container while stirring.
Continue stirring at a high speed (setting 7 or higher) until all of the chemicals are fully in solution.
In a fume hood, use a calibrated pH meter to adjust the pH to 7.4 using 1N KOH.
A fume hood is required when adjusting pH with KOH.
Adjust final volume to 1000 ml with MilliQ water using the graduation marks on the side of the container (if calibrated) or a graduated cylinder.
Remove stir bar using a magnetic stir bar remover.
Filter the ACSF through a Corning 1 liter 0.22 µm filter system.
Using Tygon tubing, attach the Corning filter system to the Gast vacuum pump. Turn on the pump.
Filter 500 ml at a time, stirring the remaining ACSF constantly on a stir plate.
Label the bottle with reagent name, date and preparer’s initials.
Can be stored at 4°C and used for up to one month.
Dispose of excess reagent directly into municipal sewer system.
Wash the stir bar with RNase Away and rinse with MilliQ water.
Technical Information:
Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid (ACSF) has a shelf life of one month at 4°C.

The osmolarity of this formulation of ACSF is normally not measured or adjusted. However, if the end user asks that it be made with a specific osmolarity, measure the osmolarity of a 10 µl sample of the solution using an osmometer prior to filtration. If the osmolarity is not in the desired range, adjust as needed.
If the osmolarity is too high, add MilliQ water.
If the osmolarity is too low, add a volume (X) of 1 mg/ml NaCl solution determined by the following equation
O= observed osmolarity
X=volume of 1 mg/ml NaCl solution to add (in ml)
Confirm that the correct osmolarity has been reached after addition of NaCl or water.
